text:
Morgan: FYI @channel — Finance asked for a Q4 GPU commit proposal by EOD Friday. I'm thinking a hybrid reserved approach: 50% reserved in us-west2, 30% reserved in eu-central1, 20% burst. Need cost delta and operational risks. :eyes:

Kai: Agree on hybrid. Quick numbers from last 30d:
- avg sustained GPUs (p50): 120
- peak daily: 220
- regional split us-west2 65%, eu-central1 25%, ap-southeast 10%
We can cover p50 with 60 reserved (us-west2) + 30 (eu-central1). Burst via spot/sustained in Dedicated. Estimated committed monthly = `60*H100_rate + 30*A100_rate` -> see calc.

Ashley: Health caveat: eu-central's cluster has network saturation on large transfers; can't push more than ~32TB/day without extra egress configs. If we move more reserved there, need 10Gbps uplink upgrade or we risk queueing and higher tail latency.

Ryan: Can you put numbers in a simple calc for finance? We need committed spend, expected savings vs on-demand, and a break-even month assuming growth 15%.

Kai: Pasting rough calc (very rough numbers for discussion):
```
// assumptions
h100_monthly_unit = 2250  // example $ per GPU-month
a100_monthly_unit = 1400
reserved_discount_multiplier = 0.60  // pay 60% of on-demand (i.e., 40% off)
planned_reserved = {us-west2:60, eu-central1:30}
committed_monthly_on_demand = 60*2250 + 30*1400 = 135000 + 42000 = 177000
committed_monthly_post_discount = committed_monthly_on_demand * reserved_discount_multiplier = 106200
// on-demand baseline (current usage) = ~177k/mo -> savings ~70.8k/mo if fully utilized
```
Numbers approximate, need billing-bot run for exacts.

billing-bot: @Morgan I've generated a 12-month forecast and attached CSV: https://billing/reports/q4-gpu-commit.csv (internal link)

Morgan: Ryan — attaching the numbers from billing-bot. Key points: committed spend ~ $106.2k/mo with 40% discount vs on-demand baseline of $177k/mo. Break-even if utilization >= 60% across reserved units; if utilization drifts below ~50% the commit becomes more expensive than incremental on-demand. Also note cross-region pricing delta (~+8% in eu-central) and slight premium for dedicated burst lanes.

Ryan: Ok, finance prefers a lower-risk start. Proposal: start with 40 reserved us-west2, 20 reserved eu-central1, keep ~15% capacity in burst/spot. That reduces commitment to ~ $78k/mo. Can you write a short justification doc (1-pager) we can send to execs with sensitivity for utilization?

Kai: Will draft. Ops note: if we start at 40/20 we should enable autoscale policies (min/max) and set per-tenant rate limits to avoid noisy tenants inflating baseline. Also suggest a canary period (2 weeks) with telemetry on tail-latency and queue length.

Ashley: Also recommend scheduling a maintenance window for the eu-central network uplink upgrade during a low-traffic weekend if execs approve extra CapEx. I'll provide the 10Gbps cost estimate tomorrow.

Morgan: I'll draft the 1-pager and include the sensitivity table for utilization levels (50/60/75/90%). Tagging legal for SLA language. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Ryan: Thx. Please include a short paragraph on fallback policy — e.g., automatic downgrade to cheaper model variants or cross-region bursting to avoid service disruption if commit capacity saturates.

Kai: Good call. I'll add fallback strategies and a note on routing policy: prefer local capacity first, then cross-region if latency budget allows.

Ashley: FYI we should also check quota requests for new reserved nodes in eu-central; customs/cloud vendor lead time might be 3-7 business days.

Morgan: Final ask: if anyone thinks APAC should get a higher share (we saw 10% last 30d but product expects growth) flag it now. Otherwise I'll send draft to Ryan by EOD Thursday.
